data.label: Vitamins in Human Body
data.summary: Essential micronutrients required for normal metabolic function, growth, and overall health.

data.label: Dietary Sources
data.summary: Various food groups that serve as primary sources of vitamins.

data.label: Fruits & Vegetables
data.summary: Rich in Vitamin C, A, and K.

data.label: Meat & Dairy
data.summary: Primary sources of B12 and D.

data.label: Grains & Nuts
data.summary: Good for Vitamin E and B-complex.

data.label: Health Impact & Balance
data.summary: The effects of vitamin levels on the body.

data.label: Deficiency
data.summary: Hypovitaminosis can lead to diseases like Scurvy or Rickets.

data.label: Excess
data.summary: Hypervitaminosis can be toxic, especially with fat-soluble vitamins.

data.label: Vitamin Classification
data.summary: Categorization of vitamins based on solubility.

data.label: Water-Soluble
data.summary: Dissolve in water; excreted easily (e.g., C, B-complex).

data.label: Fat-Soluble
data.summary: Stored in fat tissues; long-term reserves (e.g., A, D, E, K).
